text:
emi (Design): Quick review: column-pin + export microcopy for Vectors table — saw a support case where exported CSV didn't match selected columns. Need to align UI copy & selection behavior.

jonah (PM): Agreed. Current CTA says 'Export selection' but the modal defaults to 'All columns' — confusing. Suggest: CTA -> 'Export selected rows' and modal header: 'Choose columns to export'.

max (Eng): Implementation note: our front-end stores selection separately from visible columns. We can pass visibleColumns when opening export modal. Quick snippet:
```
const exportPayload = {
  rows: selectionIds,
  columns: visibleColumns || defaultColumns,
  includePinned: includePinnedFlag
}
```
This preserves order and pinned columns if we set that flag.

sara (DevEx): UX thought: prefer 'Export selected rows' as primary CTA and a more subtle link for 'Export all rows (full dataset)'. Also keyboard focus should land on the first column checkbox in the modal so screen reader users can start selecting immediately.

aria (a11y): Accessibility: ensure the modal has role="dialog" and `aria-labelledby` points to the modal header. When export completes, fire an SR alert like: 'Export ready: 12 rows' and set focus back to the export CTA. Also confirm we have visible focus styles for the checkboxes and the 'Include pinned columns' toggle.

nina (Research): From user interviews, folks expect pinned columns (ID, label) to appear by default in downloads. If we don't include them, it's surprising. Could surface a toggle: 'Include pinned columns' with a short helper: 'Pinned columns stay visible in table and can be included in exports.'

emi (Design): Love the toggle idea. Microcopy suggestions: toggle label -> 'Include pinned columns (sticky in table)'. Modal header copy -> 'Choose columns to include in export'. Default filename: change from `vectors-export-<date>.csv` to `vectors-selected-<date>.csv` so users know the file contains their selection.

max (Eng): I'll wire up passing pinnedColumns into the payload and preserve order. Quick QA question: backend accepts ordered arrays, right? We should also strip client-only columns like 'rowActions' before sending.

jonah (PM): Backend: yes, we accept ordered column lists. We'll ignore unknown columns. jonah (PM) to ops: confirm we don't allow sensitive columns in CSV export for private deployments.

emi (Design): :thumbsup: Action items: max -> PR to send visible + pinned columns and includePinned flag; aria -> add SR messages + keyboard flow checklist; sara -> final copy pass for CTA, modal header, toggle label, default filename. I'll update the design token and attach the mock to the ticket.

max (Eng): sounds good, I'll target the PR for tomorrow's sprint.

sara (DevEx): I'll run a short doc blurb for the SDK example showing `exportPayload` so customers can replicate server-side.

aria (a11y): I'll add test cases for screen reader narration and keyboard-only export flow.

emi (Design): Thanks everyone — I'll post the updated mock and follow up after PR review.
